summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and a history of venous thrombosis was admitted for evaluation of persistent nausea and malaise. She had no abdominal pain or vomiting but reported a dry cough and night sweats. Initial concerns for infection led to a brief course of antibiotics, but imaging showed a chronic retrocardiac opacity unlikely to be infectious, and antibiotics were discontinued. Nausea was thought to be related to gastroesophageal reflux, and she was started on omeprazole. A sacral fungal rash with a fissure was identified and treated with topical ketoconazole. She remained stable, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing dialysis and outpatient follow-up for a breast mass, dermatology, and primary care. Her home medications, including warfarin, insulin, and constipation regimens, were continued.
